calls.reason: NVIDIA's Warp post shows simulation uses but not how much demand they make up, and Ramp shows half of businesses pay for AI without showing whether prices cover costs. Neither settles the claim.

Tom's Guide, citing SemiAnalysis, says heavy subscribers are subsidized but the typical user stays under the break-even point. No source breaks compute down by tier, so the evidence is mixed and thin.
The forecast depends on hype receding first. The CARMA media study shows narratives shifting, not a sustained retreat, and there is no demand data from after any such retreat.
ARC Prize and METR show substantial but bounded autonomy, and METR notes remaining weaknesses. The 'never' part of the claim can't be settled by any finite record.
